name: LLCL
title: Learning to plan beyond the next frame.
summary: V-JEPA visual representations, learned action-conditioned dynamics, and planning informed by failure feedback.
description: An ongoing exploration of visual world models for sequential decisions. The system combines a V-JEPA visual encoder with a learned action-conditioned GRU and a planning loop that incorporates failure feedback.
alt: An earlier frozen JEPA agent exploring a village and fields in Veloren
mediaCaption: A selected 11-second recording of an earlier frozen JEPA agent in Veloren. Continuous capture at 30 fps, original playback speed, no audio. This clip is historical context, not a demonstration of the current system or a measure of overall performance.
mediaShortCaption: Earlier prototype recording. Selected demo, not a benchmark.
question: What does a useful visual representation need around it to support reliable decisions over several steps? LLCL studies the interaction between representation, learned dynamics and the planning procedure.
approach: A V-JEPA visual encoder supplies representations of observations. A learned action-conditioned GRU models temporal dynamics; planning uses those predictions together with failure feedback. This is a system-level investigation: a failed rollout can reflect dynamics, action alignment or planning, and does not establish an inherent flaw in V-JEPA.
verified: In a fixed-weight, 128-step ViZDoom evaluation on randomized key-door layouts, a V-JEPA-based planner explored more new cells than a reactive baseline across 16 held-out maps and three model seeds. A separate four-map core evaluation showed the same direction. The linked note gives paired estimates and limits. The Veloren recording shown here is an earlier prototype, not footage of this evaluation.
ongoing: The reported gain concerns exploration coverage. Key, door and exit success have not been demonstrated on the four core maps. The core set is small, and the on-policy training data came from one collection seed.
next: Proposed: evaluate task completion, independently collect more training data, and compare with a stronger world-model baseline.

name: MuJoCo / SketchVLA
title: Drawing as a data-generation task.
summary: A Panda arm, a whiteboard and synchronized camera views for exploring vision–language–action data in simulation.
description: A MuJoCo Panda whiteboard-drawing and VLA data project. The simulation provides a concrete setting for connecting visual observations, drawing tasks and robot actions. It is a separate project from LLCL’s world-model work.
alt: Two synchronized views of a simulated Panda arm drawing an outline on a whiteboard
mediaCaption: An existing dataset-capture recording, shown at 3× speed. Left: board-front camera. Right: eye-in-hand camera. The original 73.7-second recording is presented in about 24.6 seconds, without audio. This is simulation footage, not a trained-policy benchmark.
mediaShortCaption: Two synchronized views · 3× speed · Simulation footage.
question: How can a simple drawing task make the relationship between vision, task intent and robot motion easier to capture and inspect? A whiteboard offers a visible record of each action.
approach: A simulated Panda arm draws on a whiteboard in MuJoCo. Board-front and eye-in-hand cameras record the same sequence, allowing the scene and the local pen motion to be viewed together. The project explores this setup as a source of VLA data.
verified: The recording shows the simulation and its two synchronized views producing a drawn outline. It supports a demonstration of the capture setup; it does not establish dataset scale, trained-policy quality or generalization.
ongoing: The project remains an exploration of simulation and dataset tooling. Dataset release details and policy-evaluation results are not established in this preview.
next: A proposed next step is to document the data schema, camera alignment and capture-quality checks before presenting a dataset release or policy results.

name: SkyMerge
title: Many aerial views. One mosaic.
summary: An undergraduate UAV image-mosaicking project, taking drone imagery from camera metadata to a stitched aerial result.
description: An undergraduate project in UAV image mosaicking. SkyMerge brings metadata handling, geometric correction, feature matching, triangulation and image stitching together in a C++23 pipeline.
alt: Detail of the stitched aerial mosaic showing rows of solar panels
mediaCaption: The complete mosaic and two detail crops of the same stitched output. These are result images, not the original drone input frames. The web version is resized from the original published result.
mediaShortCaption: Crop of the published mosaic, not an input frame.
question: How can overlapping aerial images be brought into one coherent view? The project works through the geometry and implementation needed to turn separate UAV photographs into a mosaic.
approach: The pipeline reads camera metadata, corrects image rotation, matches neighboring views, triangulates structure and stitches the output. The public repository contains the implementation and configuration details.
verified: A stitched aerial mosaic and the source repository are public. The image shows one output of the pipeline; it is not a quantitative comparison of geometric accuracy, runtime or robustness.
ongoing: This page documents the existing undergraduate project and its published artifact. No new development result is claimed in this draft.
next: A proposed documentation step is to add a reproducible example with permitted source images and explicit quality measures if those materials become available.
